Subject: MedSecure — follow-up: log controls, PII redaction, residency

Alex — thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Call summary (high level):
- In-scope: request/response logging for user-facing inference calls; headers and associated metadata (trace IDs, request IDs); diagnostic/audit streams.
- Primary requirements you flagged: PII removal (names, emails, phone numbers, SSNs), redaction of sensitive headers (cookies, auth headers), deterministic handling of trace/request IDs (preserve correlation but not raw values), data residency within US regions, and strongly-limited access to raw logs.
- Retention preferences you mentioned: 90 days for request/response logs by default; 365 days for audit logs (security/infra).

Open questions we flagged on the call (please confirm):
1) Should trace/request IDs be pseudonymized (same input -> same pseudonym) or hashed + salted per-tenant so correlation works only within your account?
2) Which endpoints do you want excluded from request logging entirely (health, metrics, certain admin endpoints)?
3) Any regulatory constraints requiring immutable archival vs reversible redaction for audit purposes?

Proposed immediate next steps from our side:
- Share a short technical spec for our redaction pipeline (regex + ML-based PII classifier + token-level masking), with examples of sanitized output. (I’ll attach a spec and sample sanitized logs.)
- Provide a diagram of where logs are stored, encryption-at-rest details, and the access control model.
- Prepare a scoped POC for MedSecure in us-east-1 (we can also propose us-west-2 if you prefer), timeline: 3 weeks to POC, sample sanitized logs delivered within 5 business days of POC kickoff.
- Deliverables: Pseudonymization approach (options), retention configuration settings, and an access-control runbook for your SOC team.

Action items for you:
- Confirm whether pseudonymization should be deterministic across customers or strictly per-tenant salted.
- Share any logging exclusions and the list of internal contacts who must be able to read audit logs.

Attachments: I’m attaching the proposed spec and an anonymized sample we’ll use for the POC.

If that aligns, I’ll schedule a technical deep-dive with engineering and your security lead next week.

Thanks,
Dylan

Thanks Dylan — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side so the POC scope is tight:

1) Trace/request IDs: we need to preserve the ability to correlate across microservices but cannot accept raw IDs. Preferred approach is deterministic pseudonymization that is stable within our tenant but not reversible by Redwood engineering. We explicitly prefer a per-tenant salt.

2) Retention: we need 365 days for security/audit logs; for request/response logs a default of 90 days is acceptable, but we may request a 180-day option during trials.

3) Residency: this must be hosted in a US region (us-east-1 preferred). If the POC includes backups, we need assurance backups remain within the same region.

4) Redaction proof: our auditors will want a sample of both raw -> redacted pairs (privileged view) and a sanitized version for the app team. Can you provide a sanitized sample plus a privileged sample under an NDA or secure transfer?

5) Failure modes: describe behavior when masking fails (e.g., regex misses). We need a fallback that prevents leaking values to persistent storage (e.g., drop/pseudonymize + emit an alert to security team).

6) Access controls & key management: confirm KMS integration options and whether keys are customer-managed (bring-your-own-key).

I’ve attached our security questionnaire (initial answers in the sheet). Also include a diagram of the data flow and a short note about who at Redwood will have decryption/pseudonymization privileges if any.

Appreciate the quick turnaround here — can we aim for the POC kickoff week of 6/21?

Best,
Alex

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>

Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: MedSecure — follow-up: log controls, PII redaction, residency

Alex — great questions. Answers below and what we can commit to for the POC.

1) Pseudonymization approach
- We propose per-tenant deterministic pseudonymization: each tenant gets a unique KMS-wrapped salt. Inputs (trace/request ID) are hashed with HMAC-SHA256 + salt and then truncated to 16 bytes (base64) for storage. This preserves correlation in your account while preventing cross-tenant correlation by Redwood. Keys can be customer-managed (BYOK) if required.

2) PII redaction pipeline
- Multi-stage: (a) lightweight regex stripping for obvious patterns (SSN, credit card, phone), (b) ML-based PII classifier for contextual detection (names, free-text emails), (c) token-level masking for user message content.
- Failure mode: If both regex and ML confidence are below threshold, the pipeline will: redact the suspect span with a deterministic pseudonym and emit a high-severity alert to your security webhook (configurable). No unmasked value will be persisted.

3) Retention & storage
- Configurable retention per stream: request_logs (default 90d), audit_logs (default 365d). We can support a 180d option for request_logs for the trial period.
- Backups will be region-locked to the POC region (us-east-1) and marked with the same retention policy.

4) Access & key management
- KMS integration: support for customer-managed keys (AWS KMS CMKs), Redwood-managed KMS with strict IAM roles, or HSM-backed keys for enterprise customers.
- Decryption/pseudonymization privileges: by default, only a Red team service account has access to re-identify for support with an auditable workflow (ticket required). For MedSecure we recommend BYOK so only your SREs hold re-identification capability.

5) Deliverables & timeline
- Tech spec (attached): Proposed_Log_Pseudonymization_Spec.pdf
- Sample sanitized logs: sample_sanitized_logs_example.txt (will provide both sanitized and privileged pairs under an NDA channel)
- POC plan: kickoff week of 6/21, 3-week POC, internal milestone for sanitized sample within 5 business days of kickoff.

6) Diagram & failure behavior
- We’ll include a dataflow diagram showing collection -> preprocessor -> pseudonymization -> storage + audit stream. If masking fails, entries are pseudonymized and the raw value is not stored; an alert webhook will fire and the event will be tracked in an audit-only stream.

Next steps we propose now:
- I’ll send a calendar invite for a technical deep-dive (engineering + security) for Tues 6/22 10am PT. Please confirm attendees.
- We’ll also initiate an NDA/provision a secure transfer method for privileged log pairs — Aditya, can you own the secure share setup?

Thanks — Dylan
